title: 'He has Rs 100+ crore in bank, but...': Silicon Valley millionaire now lives in small Indian village- Moneycontrol.com
summary: An entrepreneur who built a company in Silicon Valley and became a dollar millionaire returned to India after family disputes, court cases and depression. Despite having over Rs 100 crore in the bank, he now lives in a small village, focuses on spiritual service and posts videos about healing. The story, shared on X by Vineeth K, sparked discussion about the limits of wealth and the importance of mental wellbeing.
content:
A thriving business, a fortune worth more than Rs 100 crore and a life in Silicon Valley. For many, that sounds like the definition of success. But what happens when personal struggles outweigh everything money can offer?

That is the question entrepreneur Vineeth K’s recent post on X has left many people asking. He shared the story of a former college mate who, according to him, built a successful company in Silicon Valley and became a self-made dollar millionaire. Yet, after facing family disputes, court cases and depression, the entrepreneur returned to India.

Sharing the story on X, Vineeth described his former college mate as someone who achieved significant success through his own efforts. He wrote, “One of the saddest story whenever I open my social media is of a college mate. A self-made dollar millionaire. Built a company in Silicon Valley. Earned a fortune.. But 2 years back the way, life fell apart.”

According to Vineeth, the entrepreneur had built a successful career and earned a fortune, but his personal life later became difficult. He further added, “Issues with his wife (my college mate too), her parents and brother. Court cases. Depression. His child was kept away from him…. He eventually came back to India.”

The post did not reveal the identity of the entrepreneur or provide details about the personal disputes. However, Vineeth said these challenges had a major impact on his former college mate’s life.

Vineeth said his former college mate now lives a very different life from his days in Silicon Valley. He explained, “Today, he has Rs 100+ crore in the bank, but lives in a small village, spends his time in God’s service, and shares videos about healing and surviving…. Most of the videos are not even very thoughtful, you can hear the struggle in his voice.”

Reflecting on his former college mate’s journey, Vineeth said the experience made him rethink the importance of mental wellbeing. He wrote, “I’ve seen a couple of more such cases. No amount of money can compensate for the absence of mental peace. Protect your mind as much as you protect your wealth.”

Several users shared their thoughts on Vineeth’s post, saying that peace of mind and emotional wellbeing are often overlooked. One user commented, “Mental peaceand a good night sleep are highly underrated.”

One of the saddest story whenever I open my social media is of a college mate.

A self-made dollar millionaire. Built a company in Silicon Valley. Earned a fortune.. But 2 years back the way, life fell apart. Issues with his wife (my college mate too), her parents and… — Vineeth K (@DealsDhamaka)July 26, 2026

Another added, “We cannot say when life will take a turn. We cannot escape the night.”

A user shared, “It's all easy to say protect your mind. Many times things are not in your control sir. You just need to accept and endure. The more one tries to fight and resist, the more one gets stuck. But only those who face it will understand it.”

Another user wrote, “This hits hard. Money can buy a lot of things, but not the quiet that comes from a settled mind and healthy relationships. Protecting mental peace should be non-negotiable.”
